Corrected both: PLAYING is retained until recorded completion, live records with no fixture row commit their resolved players, completion releases players/marker/board and persists it, game identity carries the fixture date and saved duties carry their own pair so a restore re-finds a re-keyed match, and an unresolvable duty is retained and shown for explicit release. node test/parse-check.cjs (312 checks) and node test/scheduler-check.cjs (694 checks) both exited 0; 12 new live-night scenarios added; local Chromium harness confirmed the retained-duty affordance and its one-click release.

The RECOMMENDED-pane confirmation now persists immediately even with Managed Boards OFF. derivePlayerStates keeps PLAYING and flags the stale duty as a conflict. RECOMMENDED and PROJECTED NEXT names and marker names are 1.5px larger and semibold with a height-neutral row, scoped away from TONIGHT and DELAYED. node test/parse-check.cjs (322 checks) and node test/scheduler-check.cjs (731 checks) both exited 0. No live-service or venue-night validation was performed.

history.work_package: PROJECTED NEXT reconciled against proposed marking duties (observed browser-test conflict: a proposed marker also named as the next match player)
history.phase: V1.1.0 release candidate plus scheduler slice 1
history.verification: Cause: getProjectedRunningOrder builds every wave before any marker proposal exists, so plan.projectedNextPriorities never saw the duty the RECOMMENDED pane proposes; the player was named as the next match's player while his marking duty would still be active. Corrected with a temporary projected-commitment replay: the plan's own opening wave is replayed with the proposed duty holders held out of a COPY of the session, and the first genuinely free next match is shown instead; when every planned next match needs somebody who is still marking, the pane states the wait instead of naming an impossible game. Nothing is reserved, confirmed or persisted, the RECOMMENDED wave is never re-planned, and confirmed duties already reach the plan as factual MARKING/RESERVED. node test/parse-check.cjs (325 checks) and node test/scheduler-check.cjs (749 checks) both exited 0; 18 new PROJECTED NEXT checks cover the observed scene, alternative selection, withheld count, RECOMMENDED immutability, plan arithmetic, confirmed duty, release, marker change, FAIR and LOSER consistency, NORMAL and OPTIMISED with managed boards ON/OFF, OFF/MANUAL unchanged and a full venue. Measured on the captured payload the reconciliation adds 1.85 ms to a 76 ms OPTIMISED advice build. Not validated on a live venue night.

history.work_package: RECOMMENDED pane treated as one dispatch group: no player proposed to mark while recommended to play in the same pane (observed browser-test conflict, Drew Tyler)
history.phase: V1.1.0 release candidate plus scheduler slice 1
history.verification: Cause: the marker candidate pool excluded only the participants of the first `nextCapacity` recommended games (free board slots), while the pane is the whole opening wave. When free boards are fewer than the pane's rows (a partly occupied venue), the 'waiting for a board' tail rows stayed markable, so a foot-row player could be proposed as the marker of a row above him - reproduced deterministically before the change (freeBoards 3, 4 rows, foot-row player proposed as marker for row 1) and gone after it. Corrected by widening the exclusion to every game in the RECOMMENDED pane, in the automatic allocation and in the operator dropdown's shared reservation (markerSequenceReservedIds), so the two can never disagree. Matches after the pane (PROJECTED NEXT and later) stay markable, nothing is persisted or reserved permanently, OFF and MANUAL are untouched, and the FAIR/LOSER ordering, the LOSER duty preference and the PROJECTED NEXT duty reconciliation are unchanged. node test/parse-check.cjs (325 checks) and node test/scheduler-check.cjs (770 checks) both exited 0; test 124 adds 21 checks covering the observed scene, the old window that permitted it, alternative marker selection, genuine NO MARKER when the pane is the whole roster, dropdown agreement, confirmed duty plus refresh restoration, FAIR and LOSER under NORMAL and OPTIMISED with managed boards ON/OFF, and OFF/MANUAL unchanged; test 109's reserved-set assertions were re-based deliberately from the next-N prefix to the whole pane. On the captured payload (46-player roster, 20 fixtures on 5 Nov) the wider exclusion removed the play-and-mark conflict at 2 and 3 live games while all four recommended rows stayed covered by markers, and at 0-1 live games (where it is a no-op) the behaviour is byte-identical; timing differences on that payload were within the +/-40% run-to-run noise of the harness and OFF (which skips the reconciliation entirely) showed the same spread, so no performance claim is made. Not validated on a live venue night.
resolves: Confirm the intended meaning of 'the next N projected games' for the marker list (implemented as the next N dispatchable games, N = free boards, matching the scheduler's own MARKER-4 rule)
